note: RFC 5492 Section 5 says: The Data field in the NOTIFICATION message MUST list the set of capabilities that causes the speaker to send the message. Each such capability is encoded in the same way as it would be encoded in the OPEN message. Both current actual-OPEN matrices retain every prior input and exact wire assertion. Refused capability and required/refused ADD-PATH family settings are now installed before Accept freezes the proposal, so both handleOpen and processOpen reach the intended admission rule. Fourteen generic cases require exact code 2/7 and original local-required or peer-refused ASN4, repeated Graceful Restart, ADD-PATH and hostname values while excluding satisfied or unrelated capabilities. Eight family cases require the causing family's original direction and capability grouping, including exact complete 3771-octet NOTIFICATIONs from legal extended OPENs. The existing causing-set unit independently checks both missing capabilities, only the still-missing one, unknown-code exclusion and useful acceptance; builder units check original ASN4 and empty-valued tuples and no-causes nil. Current producers select actual OPEN capabilities and use their OPEN encoders, retaining repeated instances and bounded ADD-PATH grouping. No expected value or rejection assertion was weakened. The wire and builder controls would fail on missing, extra, substituted, reversed or flattened causing data.
